 The rains have started in San Francisco, and this year is poised to be a dramatic one for inclement weather. 
 We originally published this comic from our intern Ronna Raz during last year’s rains — a deep dive into sewer infrastructure and municipal flooding. We are republishing it for our “Super El Niño” season. 
 We have a $130,000 match! 
 Double your gift! 
 Every few years during the rainy season, certain neighborhoods of San Francisco flood. 
 If it rains too hard or for too long, the sewer pipes fill, pushing water (and raw sewage) out of floor drains and sewer grates.
 Residents and businesses near 17th and Folsom streets in the Mission spend every winter anxiously  preparing  for floods. City workers line the  sidewalks  with plastic barriers, and residents  improvise  their  own designs . The damage is so costly, at that intersection and elsewhere , that sometimes businesses shutter. 
 Why do San Francisco’s sewers do this?
